input.paper_title: Graph-Aware Prompting for Reliable Section Generation
input.paper_venue: ACL Workshop on Natural Language Generation
input.paper_abstract: We present a graph-guided prompting workflow for long-form scientific writing that prioritizes evidence and citation consistency. Our method constructs a document graph that encodes section dependencies and uses strict JSON schemas and evidence-aware prompts to generate and validate individual sections. At generation time, the system (1) builds a section graph and schedules leaf-first writing, (2) retrieves and injects relevant evidence for each section, (3) produces JSON-constrained section outputs, and (4) assembles a LaTeX manuscript with refs.bib. We evaluate the approach by comparing it to a baseline linear prompting pipeline on two topical domains, measuring citation coverage, hallucination rate, and reviewer-style scores. Results show improved citation coverage and reduced unsupported assertions while keeping edits and post-hoc audits straightforward via machine-readable outputs. We intentionally state conservative claims and require explicit source citations for all factual assertions. The paper contributes practical artifacts: a graph-based section scheduler, an evidence-injection protocol per section, and an audit-friendly JSON output format that integrates with standard LaTeX/bib workflows. Our experiments use internal notes and a small curated PDF set where available; metrics focus on citation fidelity and factual consistency rather than broad generalization.

input.section_title: JSON schema and evidence-aware prompt templates
input.section_summary: Specify the JSON output schema used to represent generated sections (fields, types, and required citation entries), plus the evidence-aware prompt templates that enforce citation insertion and schema conformance during generation. Include schema validation points and examples of required fields without providing full schemas.

output:
This section specifies the design principles and concrete elements of the JSON representation we use for individual generated sections, and the evidence-aware prompt templates that enforce citation insertion and schema conformance during generation. We do not reproduce the full machine-readable schema here; rather, we describe the required fields, types, validation checkpoints, and exemplar prompt fragments sufficient for reproduction and audit.

Design goals. The JSON schema is intended to (1) make the generated text machine-interpretable for post-hoc validation and assembly into LaTeX, (2) bind factual assertions to explicit evidence and bibliographic entries, and (3) record provenance and generation metadata to support audits and incremental edits. The schema therefore combines three logical groups of fields: textual content, citation/evidence bindings, and metadata/validation records.

Core field groups (conceptual description).
- section_identity: identifiers and human-readable titles used during graph scheduling and final assembly (types: string id, string title).
- content: the primary written output for the section (type: string). The content field is intended to contain a LaTeX-safe fragment (escaped as needed) that will be inserted into the manuscript during assembly.
- assertions: an optional list of extracted or explicitly marked factual claims contained in the content. Each assertion is an object with fields (text: string; citations: list of citation keys; provenance_snippets: list of evidence references). The assertions field is used by automated checks that map claims to evidence.
- citations: a list of bibliographic entries referenced by the section (type: list of objects). Each citation object minimally includes a local bibkey (string) and a compact bibliographic record (string) or an explicit pointer to a refs.bib entry to be included in assembly.
- evidence_snippets: a ranked list of retrieved evidence items injected into prompts (type: list of objects). Each snippet records source_id (identifier for the source document), excerpt_text (string), snippet_score (numeric), and source_locator (e.g., page or paragraph; string).
- generation_metadata: metadata about the generation step (model name/version, prompt template id, generation timestamp, random seed or request id; types: strings and timestamps).
- validation: a post-generation validation object that records schema conformance (enum), citation_coverage (boolean or fraction), unsupported_assertions (list), and validation_issues (list of strings). This field is populated by downstream validators and auditors.
- latex_fragment: optional pre-rendered LaTeX fragment corresponding to content (string). If present, assembly can use this directly; otherwise, content is converted/escaped at assembly time.

Example minimal JSON fragment (illustrative; not a complete schema):
\begin{verbatim}
{
  "section_identity": {"id": "3-3", "title": "JSON schema and prompts"},
  "content": "We require that each factual statement is paired with an explicit citation marker ...",
  "assertions": [
    {"text": "Each factual statement must cite a source.",
     "citations": ["doe2020-method"],
     "provenance_snippets": ["src:pdf-12:para3"]}
  ],
  "citations": [
    {"bibkey": "doe2020-method", "record": "..."}
  ],
  "evidence_snippets": [
    {"source_id": "pdf-12", "excerpt_text": "...", "snippet_score": 0.92}
  ],
  "generation_metadata": {"model": "internal-vX", "prompt_id": "evidence-aware-v1"},
  "validation": {"schema_conformant": true, "unsupported_assertions": []}
}
\end{verbatim}
(We omit full type constraints and enumerations from this excerpt; the implemented schema used in experiments enforces types and required fields programmatically.)

Validation checkpoints. We apply a sequence of conservative checks after generation:
- Schema conformance: ensure required top-level keys are present and types match the declared schema (e.g., content is a non-empty string; citations is a list).
- Citation presence: for any entry under assertions where the content appears to be a factual claim, require at least one citation key in the assertion.citations list; flag assertions without citations as unsupported.
- Citation-to-bib consistency: every citation key referenced anywhere in assertions or content must appear in the citations list; missing bib entries are treated as validation failures.
- Evidence provenance: each provenance_snippets entry must include a source_id and either a source_locator or an attached excerpt_text; missing provenance is permitted only under explicit human-reviewed exceptions.
- Assembly safety: if latex_fragment is absent, convert content to LaTeX-safe form and verify that citation markers conform to the assembly convention (e.g., citation markers are matched to bibkeys).
Validation failures are surfaced with structured messages in validation.validation_issues and recorded for downstream human review.

Evidence-aware prompt templates. Prompts used for generation follow a small set of template components that are assembled per-section. Each prompt explicitly (a) provides the section context from the document graph, (b) injects ranked evidence snippets, (c) states the JSON output schema contract, and (d) enforces citation behavior and provenance recording. A compact template skeleton used by the system is shown below (brackets indicate filler slots):

- System instruction (role-level brief): produce a JSON object conforming to the provided schema; be conservative in factual claims and require explicit citation(s) for each factual sentence.
- Context block: [section_identity and, optionally, parent_section_summaries]
- Evidence injection block: up to N top-ranked snippets prefixed with their source identifiers and snippet_score.
- Output contract: explicit JSON schema excerpt (required keys and types) and a short example of the expected JSON structure.
- Citation instruction: specify the citation marker format to use in content (for example, use inline bibkeys of the form [@bibkey] or LaTeX \texttt{\textbackslash cite\{bibkey\}}); require that every assertion has a corresponding entry in the ``citations'' list.
- Generation constraints: maximum output length, maximum number of assertions to extract, and a final validation step instruction: ``After generation, return only the JSON object; do not include explanatory text.''

Illustrative prompt fragment (verbatim-style; presented here in prose for clarity):
- ``You are asked to write the section with id [id] and title '[title]'. Use the evidence snippets below to support factual statements. For any factual assertion you make, insert an inline citation marker of the form [@bibkey] and add the corresponding bibliographic entry to the 'citations' list. Return a single JSON object conforming to the following minimal contract: keys 'section_identity', 'content', 'assertions', 'citations', 'evidence_snippets', 'generation_metadata', and 'validation'. Do not output any text outside the JSON object.''

Implementation notes and conservative defaults. To reduce risks of unsupported assertions we adopt conservative defaults in the template:
- Prefer snippet quoting: the prompt encourages direct quoting when a precise claim is derived from a snippet and asks the generator to include provenance_snippets entries.
- Mandatory assertion-level citations: the template instructs the model to attach at least one citation per assertion.
- Post-generation self-check instruction: the prompt requests the model to run a brief self-check and populate validation fields before returning the JSON.
- Failure behavior: if the model cannot confidently support a factual statement from provided evidence, the prompt should instruct it to (a) omit the statement, or (b) mark it as speculative in assertions with an explicit ``speculative'': true flag. Such speculative items are then flagged for human review during validation.

Failure modes and mitigations (brief). Common failure modes include omission of required keys, citation keys present in-text but missing from the citations list, and overly synthetic assertions that lack direct evidence linkage. These are addressed by the validation checkpoints above and by (a) rejecting non-conformant JSON automatically, and (b) surfacing detailed validation_issues for targeted human remediation.

Reproducibility. The schema fragments, prompt templates, and validator code used in our experiments are provided with the project artifacts (see supplementary materials). Where stricter institutional or publisher workflows require alternative citation formats, the prompt templates and the small schema mapping layer can be adapted to enforce different in-text citation conventions and bib formats.

Notes. The descriptions above present the intent and key elements of the JSON schema and evidence-aware prompts used in our workflow. The paper's supplementary materials contain the full machine-readable schema and canonical prompt templates used in experiments; those artifacts enable deterministic validation and automatic assembly into LaTeX with refs.bib.
